citations.desc: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
citations.narrative:
The IACUC reviewed and approved Protocol #2025.02.001, a veterinary teaching protocol in which 6-9 month old bovine
calves receive improperly administered injections intended to create lesions prior to euthanasia and necropsy 3-7 days
after injection. The protocol states that the lesions “…may be characterized by swelling, heat, reluctance to move, and/or
reduced feed intake.” Although the protocol includes administration of a pain-relieving drug for such symptoms, these
clinical signs are not consistent with brief or momentary pain or distress, which would elevate the pain classification
beyond a Category C for this protocol and, therefore, necessitate a literary search for alternatives. The protocol does not
contain a literature search for alternatives. The IACUC chair and research compliance administrator / IACUC protocol
administrator were re-trained on the necessary components for protocol submission and the protocol was closed on
6/29/2026.
Literature searches for alternatives are important components for inclusion in all protocols that cause more than
momentary or slight pain or distress to the animals, in order for the IACUC to fully review proposed activities and
determine if what is proposed is acceptable. The registrant must ensure that all principal investigators consider
alternatives to procedures that may cause more than momentary or slight pain or distress to the animals and that they
provide a written narrative description of the methods and sources used to determine that alternatives were not available.
CORRECTED AT THE TIME OF INSPECTION

citations.desc: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
citations.narrative:
The IACUC reviewed and approved Protocol #2025.02.001, a veterinary teaching protocol in which 6-9 month old bovine
calves “…will be injected with typical products used in bovine medicine that can result in carcass lesions when
administered in an extralable fashion. After 3-5 days, the animals will be euthanized and necropsied to show students the
lesions created by the injections.” A list of the drugs to be utilized is not provided anywhere in the protocol. The IACUC
chair and research compliance administrator / IACUC protocol administrator were re-trained on the necessary
components for protocol submission and the protocol was closed on 6/29/2026.
Details such as substances administered to animals are necessary because it is important that proposals to conduct
animal activity contain enough detail for the IACUC to determine if the likelihood of pain or discomfort exists and to
consider if/how pain and discomfort might be limited to that which is unavoidable for the conduct of scientifically valuable
research. The registrant must ensure that all protocols reviewed by the IACUC contain a complete description of use,
including pertinent information regarding the names and routes of administration of administered substances, in order to
help anticipate and, if possible, mitigate preventable pain or discomfort.
CORRECTED AT THE TIME OF INSPECTION
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
